A network failure produces unreachable, never deprecated or closed.

limitations: Rules can be changed by the parent. Read them at the height you are claiming at, not from a cached page.

pages.title: Confirmations and reorgs
pages.description: When an Atomicals result is settled enough to act on, and what changes when the chain reorganises.

pages.title: Create a Container

limitations: No Universe read projection exposes Containers. Verification of your own collection uses the reference CLI or a compatible indexer.

pages.title: Create DMINT items
pages.description: Seal the manifest before opening minting, and check what is on chain before making it permanent.
limitations: Sealing is permanent. A manifest sealed with a mistake cannot be corrected.

pages.title: Deploy a fixed DFT
pages.description: Publish the mint rules others will claim against, and get the four parameters right the first time.

pages.title: Deploy a perpetual DFT
pages.description: An activation gated mode with progressing Bitwork, and the display rule that stops you publishing a supply cap that does not exist.

pages.title: Direct FT issuance
pages.description: One transaction, one complete supply, and the bitcoin you must actually commit for it.
limitations: No Universe product surface exposes direct FT issuance. This procedure uses the reference CLI.

pages.title: Fees and costs
pages.description: Everything you actually pay for an Atomicals action, including the costs people forget until they have already spent them.
limitations: Marketplace fee amounts are deployment configuration, not protocol behavior. Read the fee disclosure in the flow you are using.

pages.title: Inspect an ARC-20 ticker
pages.description: Resolve a name to the Atomical that actually holds it, and read the deployment before you trust any figure about it.
limitations: Resolution is computed at a chain position. Re-resolve before acting rather than trusting a cached answer.

pages.title: Inspect an address
pages.description: Read outpoints instead of totals, and understand exactly what a balance figure hides.

pages.title: Inspect an Atomical
pages.description: Read identity, location, history, and sealed state, and know which of the four you are actually looking at.

pages.title: List an ARC-20 lot
pages.description: Prove ownership, prepare a listing, sign it, and finalise, without exposing the asset to an unbound signature.
limitations: Every marketplace action gate defaults to off. A capability being documented is not a statement that it is enabled on a deployment.

pages.title: List an NFT, Realm, or Subrealm
pages.description: The same lifecycle as an ARC-20 lot, plus the extra name check the Realm lanes carry.

pages.title: Mint an Atomicals NFT
pages.description: Build the payload, choose an output value, and understand which decisions become permanent.

pages.title: Mint ARC-20
pages.description: Claim against a deployment without wasting a fee on a claim that was never going to be valid.
limitations: A confirmed Bitcoin transaction is not a successful mint. Quota, height, and Bitwork are checked by the validator, not by Bitcoin.

pages.title: Offers
pages.description: Make an offer, cancel it, and accept one, with the checks each side owes the other.

pages.title: Prepare BTC and protected UTXOs
pages.description: Build a cardinal pool for fees so a coloured output is never selected by accident, and size your lots for the transfers you expect.

pages.title: Protect coloured outputs
pages.description: The working separation between asset money and fee money, and the three habits that prevent an accidental spend.

pages.title: Recover from a rejection
pages.description: A transaction that has not confirmed is still recoverable. Here is how to work out which situation you are in.

pages.title: Resolve Unicode names
pages.description: Normalise, compare, and detect confusable names before you act on one.
limitations: Confusable detection reduces risk. What looks alike depends on the font and the reader, so it cannot eliminate it.

pages.title: Split and combine ARC-20
pages.description: Reshape your lots deliberately, and know when combining makes future transfers harder.

pages.title: Transfer ARC-20
pages.description: Build a transfer that places every unit where you intend and burns nothing.
limitations: The Universe visible transfer surface does not construct partial recipient allocations or coloured change from an amount field. Use a compatible builder that works in outpoints and output values.

pages.title: Unavailable index or empty balance
pages.description: The difference between a service that cannot answer and an answer of zero, and why confusing them causes most false alarms.

pages.title: Update or remove a listing
pages.description: Change a price or delist, with the same ownership proof and the same failure-closed checks.

pages.title: Verify a transaction
pages.description: Confirm what a transaction actually did, before signing and after broadcast, including any burn it caused.

pages.title: Verify settlement
pages.description: Confirm a trade actually completed, on chain and in the index, rather than trusting a status label.

pages.title: Wallet signing failures
pages.description: Diagnose a wallet that will not sign, by capability, encoding, and signature hash flag.
limitations: Provider capabilities vary between wallets and versions. Discover capability before building, rather than after a failure.

pages.title: Atomicals and ARC-20
pages.description: Protocol reference, task guides, API contracts, and safety tools for Atomicals digital objects and ARC-20 tokens on Bitcoin.

pages.title: Atomicals Improvement Proposals
pages.description: The AIP register, the complete status model, and implementation evidence that is never assumed from a proposal existing.
limitations: The register reflects the vendored snapshot at the pinned revision. A proposal added upstream since then is not shown until the snapshot is refreshed by CI.
An AIP is never marked implemented because it exists. Only the evidence file can establish that.

pages.title: Allocation
pages.description: The exact rule a validator uses to place coloured value into outputs, with executed vectors for every case.
limitations: The engine behind these vectors models normal allocation. It is explanatory and never a substitute for validating a concrete transaction against your target validator revision.

pages.title: ARC-20 Bitwork requirements
pages.description: Which Bitwork fields apply to a deployment, which apply to its claimants, and how to read them correctly.

pages.title: Burns
pages.description: How ARC-20 value is destroyed, the four shapes that cause it, and the checks that prevent every one of them.
limitations: A confirmed burn is permanent. Nothing in this documentation can reverse one.

pages.title: Decentralised mint claims
pages.description: What makes a dmt claim valid, why a confirmed claim can still be worthless, and what a minter should check first.
limitations: Claim validity depends on the state of the deployment at the height of the claim. A claim built against stale deployment state can confirm and still be invalid.

pages.title: Direct FT issuance
pages.description: One transaction, one complete supply, entirely in output zero, and why that makes large supplies expensive.
limitations: No Universe product surface exposes direct FT issuance. This page documents protocol behavior only.

pages.title: Fixed DFT deployment
pages.description: The parameters a fixed decentralised deployment sets, what they bound, and what a client must check before treating one as valid.
limitations: Do not present a fixed deployment as valid without checking the target network's active rules.

pages.title: Metadata and decimals
pages.description: Optional metadata fields, how to treat them, and the exact rule about decimals that prevents an entire class of accounting bug.

pages.title: ARC-20
pages.description: The complete ARC-20 model in one page, from issuance through allocation to the safety boundary, with links to the exact rule for each part.
limitations: This is a compatibility guide, not an independent consensus specification. The Atomicals specification is defined in code.

pages.title: Perpetual DFT
pages.description: A separate activation gated mode with progressing Bitwork and an optional global cap, and why it is not fixed DFT with a large number.
limitations: Do not display a fixed supply cap for a perpetual deployment unless the actual deployment and the active implementation establish one.

pages.title: PSBT requirements
pages.description: What a partially signed transaction must contain for an Atomicals aware wallet to sign it safely, and what a wallet must show you.
limitations: Wallet support for specific signature hash flags and PSBT encodings varies. Verify capability before building, not after a signing failure.

pages.title: Split and combine
pages.description: Separating coloured lots with the split operation, recombining them, and the activation gated custom coloring path.
limitations: Split and custom coloring payload shapes are implementation specific. Do not hand-assemble them from a user interface amount field.

pages.title: Substantiation Factor
pages.description: What this material is, what status it has, and what evidence would be required before any of it could be presented as behavior.
limitations: No applicable source revision or conformance suite was located that establishes Substantiation Factor as implemented behavior. This page therefore states status only.

pages.title: Tickers and candidates
pages.description: How an ARC-20 name is requested, resolved, and displayed, and what winning it actually means.
limitations: The ticker character rule is a fact about the pinned revision. Validate names against the exact active target rather than hardcoding a display rule.

pages.title: Transfers and swaps
pages.description: Ordinary transfers, atomic swaps, and the exact output binding that makes a swap safe to sign.
limitations: Swap safety depends on the signature hash flags and the exact outputs each party commits to. A swap constructed without exact output binding is not safe to sign.

pages.title: The unit model
pages.description: One coloured satoshi is one unit, supply is measured in satoshis, and decimals are presentation only.

pages.title: Wallet safety
pages.description: What an Atomicals aware wallet must do, what it must never do, and how to tell whether the wallet you use qualifies.

pages.title: AVM opcodes
pages.description: The complete opcode inventory generated from the interpreter source, with the upstream test annotation preserved per opcode.
limitations: The status column reflects the upstream source comment only. It is not a Universe verification result.
Opcodes with no upstream annotation are shown as such rather than assumed working.

pages.title: AVM
pages.description: The Atomicals Virtual Machine, split into the four separate status layers people usually collapse into one.
limitations: No Universe service executes AVM contracts. No Universe attestation of AVM behavior has been published.
Upstream test annotations describe the interpreter's own test suite, not production deployment.

pages.title: AVM state and execution
pages.description: What a contract call receives, what it returns, and how state is expected to be carried between calls.
limitations: This page describes the upstream beta interpreter's model. No Universe deployment runs it, so none of it is verified against Universe infrastructure.

pages.title: AVM status and limitations
pages.description: The exact status of every AVM layer, the threat model, and the evidence that would be required to change any of it.
limitations: No Universe service executes AVM contracts, publishes an AVM API, or attests to AVM behavior.

pages.title: DMINT
pages.description: Decentralised item minting against a sealed manifest, how verification works, and every failure state a claimant can hit.
limitations: Manifest structure and rule evaluation are implementation specific. Build manifests with the reference tooling rather than by hand.

pages.title: Item verification
pages.description: How to prove an item belongs to a Container, what each check establishes, and what a product must show.

pages.title: Containers
pages.description: A named collection identity that items can prove membership in, and what it takes to make that proof meaningful.
limitations: No Universe read projection exposes Containers or DMINT items today. This section documents protocol behavior only.

pages.title: Sealing and rules
pages.description: What sealing changes, why rule evaluation must be deterministic, and the order of operations that makes a collection trustworthy.

pages.title: Activation boundaries
pages.description: Why the same transaction can be valid at one height and invalid at another, and how to reason about rules that turn on.
limitations: Activation heights are defined per network in the reference implementation. A behavior proven on one network says nothing about another.

pages.title: Bitwork
pages.description: The proof of work prefix requirement that gates Atomicals mints, what it costs, and what it does not promise.
limitations: Estimates are probabilistic. No amount of work guarantees a result in any particular time, and nothing here is a profitability statement.

pages.title: Candidates and winners
pages.description: Why a name request is not a name, how a candidate becomes a verified winner, and what a product must show while resolution is pending.
limitations: Confirmation depth requirements and tie-breaking are version sensitive. Read the deployment and the active revision rather than assuming a fixed number of blocks.

pages.title: Commit and reveal
pages.description: The two transaction pattern every Atomicals operation uses, and what can go wrong between the two steps.
limitations: Bitwork applies to the commit transaction id, the reveal transaction id, or both, depending on the operation and the deployment configuration.

pages.title: Confirmation and reorgs
pages.description: Two separate questions that people constantly merge into one, and what a reorg actually does to an Atomicals result.

pages.title: Atomicals digital objects
pages.description: What an Atomical actually is at the data level, what a validator stores about it, and what it never guarantees.

pages.title: Envelope and operations
pages.description: The structure a validator reads, the operation codes it recognises, and why a JSON object in a user interface is not a wire format.
limitations: Operation availability and payload validation are activation sensitive. Build against the exact revision you target.

pages.title: Identifiers and numbers
pages.description: Atomical IDs, compact IDs, locations, numbers, and which one to store in your database.

pages.title: Indexer and validator dependency
pages.description: Why every Atomicals answer is version scoped, and how to handle two sources that disagree.
limitations: Two sources agreeing does not prove either is right. It proves they share an interpretation.

pages.title: Metadata trust boundaries
pages.description: Everything in a payload is attacker controlled. This page says exactly what that means for a renderer, an indexer, and a user interface.

pages.title: Permanent file storage
pages.description: How Atomicals stores bytes on Bitcoin, what a digest proves, and the limits of treating a chain as a file system.
limitations: Permanence describes the bytes in a block. It does not promise that any particular service will serve, decode, or render them.

pages.title: References and recursion
pages.description: How one Atomical points at another, why recursive rendering needs an archive, and the failure modes of a broken reference.
limitations: Recursive rendering depends on the renderer resolving every dependency. A renderer that cannot reach a dependency produces a different result from one that can, without either being wrong about the chain data.

pages.title: State, history, and updates
pages.description: How mutable state works on an Atomical, what history records, and what sealing permanently changes.

pages.title: UTXO ownership and location
pages.description: Ownership in Atomicals is control of a specific unspent output, not an entry against an address.
limitations: Address level views are conveniences built on top of outpoint level truth. They can lag or aggregate incorrectly without being wrong about any single outpoint.

pages.title: Collections and Containers
pages.description: How an NFT proves membership in a collection, what a Container adds, and what a collection label alone proves.

pages.title: NFT marketplace behavior
pages.description: What the Marketplace authority checks before an NFT listing, purchase, or settlement is allowed to proceed.
limitations: Every marketplace action gate defaults to off. A capability being documented does not mean it is enabled on any deployment.

pages.title: Metadata and media
pages.description: How an NFT carries files, what a digest guarantees, and the rules a renderer must follow to serve hostile content safely.
limitations: A digest proves byte integrity only. It says nothing about rights, originality, or whether the content is safe to render.

pages.title: Minting an NFT
pages.description: What a mint payload contains, what output zero receives, and the decisions that cannot be changed later.

pages.title: Atomicals NFTs
pages.description: Non-fungible Atomicals, what they carry, how they move, and the hazards that come from sharing an output.
limitations: The Universe read model projects plain NFTs, Realms, and Subrealms. Containers and DMINT items are excluded from that projection by declaration.

pages.title: Splat and mixed outputs
pages.description: What happens when one output carries several Atomicals, why that is dangerous, and how splat separates them.

pages.title: NFT transfers
pages.description: Normal transfers, swap transfers, and what a non-fungible move actually commits to.

pages.title: Atomicals protocol
pages.description: One page that puts every Atomicals primitive, operation, and validation boundary in relation to each other.
limitations: The Atomicals specification is defined in code. This page summarises one pinned revision and is not an independent consensus specification.

pages.title: Claims and rules
pages.description: How a name claim is evaluated, how payments participate, and why deterministic rules are the whole point.

pages.title: Realm marketplace behavior
pages.description: What the Marketplace authority checks for Realm and Subrealm listings, and why names have an extra verification step.
limitations: Every marketplace action gate defaults to off. Documentation of a capability is not a statement that it is enabled.

pages.title: Realms
pages.description: Top-level Atomicals names, how they are claimed and resolved, and what a name actually establishes.
limitations: A name proves allocation, never identity. Two names that look identical to a reader can be different strings.

pages.title: Paynames
pages.description: Using a Realm as a payment destination, what resolution guarantees, and the checks a payer must run first.
limitations: Resolution is computed at a chain position and by one implementation. A payer who resolves once and caches the answer can pay the wrong destination later.

pages.title: Subrealms
pages.description: Child names claimed under a parent Realm's rules, how the parent controls them, and what a claimant must satisfy.

pages.title: Unicode, IDNA, and confusable names
pages.description: Why two names that look identical can be different strings, what normalisation does, and the warnings a product must show.
limitations: Confusable detection reduces risk. It cannot eliminate it, because what looks alike depends on the font and the reader.

pages.title: AI and agent access
pages.description: Every machine readable output this documentation publishes, and what each one is for.

pages.title: Universe ARC-20 API
pages.description: The complete ARC-20 read contract, with its guarantees, its declared coverage limit, and the OpenAPI document behind it.
limitations: Declared coverage is partial. The limitation applies to pending activity only, not to the confirmed scan or the holder proof requirements.

pages.title: Universe NFT and Realm API
pages.description: The complete read contract for plain NFTs, Realms, and Subrealms, including what the projection deliberately excludes.
limitations: The projection excludes fungible tokens, Containers, and DMINT items by declaration. An empty answer for one of those is correct, not a failure.

pages.title: Marketplace v1
pages.description: The complete lifecycle, the signing contract, the exact PSBT shape, and everything the authority refuses.
limitations: Every marketplace and action gate defaults to false. Documentation of a capability is not a statement that it is enabled on any deployment.
Internal bridge routes are documented so integrators understand the boundary. They are not publicly reachable and no credential value appears here.

pages.title: Ordex contract
pages.description: Where the Ordex marketplace contract, SDK, conformance vectors, and verifier live, and how the Universe boundary sits around them.
limitations: This page links the Ordex contract rather than restating it. A restated copy would drift, and a drifted copy of a settlement contract is dangerous.

pages.title: Atomicals CLI reference
pages.description: Every command in the reference CLI, generated from the pinned source so the inventory cannot drift.
limitations: Command availability and behavior depend on the CLI revision you run and the validator it talks to. This inventory describes one pinned revision.
Options that change wallet or signing behavior are noted per command below, but the CLI itself is the authority on what it does.

pages.title: TypeScript client
pages.description: A generated, strictly typed client for the public read APIs, with typed errors, pagination helpers, and no embedded secrets.
limitations: The client covers the public read surfaces and the safe Marketplace contract types. It does not sign, broadcast, or hold key material.

pages.title: Conformance vectors
pages.description: The deterministic cases that back the prose, the interactive tools, and the tests, all executed from one engine.
limitations: The allocation engine models normal allocation and the activation gated custom coloring path. It is explanatory and never a substitute for validating a concrete transaction against your target validator revision.

Vectors for lifecycle behavior that depends on a live chain or a live service are described here as expectations rather than published as executed vectors, because executing them would require infrastructure this documentation deliberately does not carry.

pages.title: ElectrumX reference
pages.description: The Atomicals ElectrumX interface, what a Universe proxy adds, and where the boundary between them sits.
limitations: Method availability and response shapes are version sensitive. Confirm against the exact release you connect to.
A Universe proxy or gateway is not the same as official ElectrumX. Do not attribute proxy behavior to the protocol.

pages.title: Documentation MCP server
pages.description: A local, read-only server that lets an agent query this documentation without scraping HTML.
limitations: The server is read only by construction. It exposes no mutation, signing, broadcast, wallet, or operator capability, and it requires no credential.

pages.title: OpenAPI and downloads
pages.description: Validated OpenAPI 3.1 documents, JSON Schemas, and every machine readable artefact this site publishes.
limitations: No production host is published in any document. Set the server variable to the origin your deployment exposes.

pages.title: JSON Schemas
pages.description: The shared component library, what each definition is for, and the rules it encodes.

pages.title: Wallet integration
pages.description: Provider detection, capability discovery, PSBT encodings, signing scopes, and normalised errors.
limitations: Provider methods and payload shapes vary between wallets and versions. Only build against capabilities the current provider contract actually proves.

pages.title: Releases
pages.description: What changed in this documentation, when, and why, with the machine readable feed alongside.

pages.title: Deprecations
pages.description: What is scheduled for removal, what replaces it, and what a deprecation does and does not promise.

pages.title: Migrations
pages.description: Step by step moves between versions, and the general procedure for any upgrade.

pages.title: Versions and compatibility
pages.description: Every pinned source revision, what it applies to, and how the baselines relate to each other.

pages.title: Choose your path
pages.description: Four short routes through this documentation, one for each thing people actually come here to do.

pages.title: Glossary
pages.description: Every Atomicals and ARC-20 term used on this site, defined once and used consistently everywhere.

pages.title: Networks and versions
pages.description: Which network a statement applies to, which validator revision decides it, and which documentation version you are reading.
limitations: Activation heights differ per network. A behavior proven on one network does not prove the same behavior on another.

pages.title: Protocol family map
pages.description: Every Atomicals primitive in one place, what it produces, which operation creates it, and where Universe exposes it today.
limitations: Support columns describe Universe product exposure at the verified date, not protocol capability.

pages.title: Safety fundamentals
pages.description: The eight checks that separate a clean Atomicals transaction from a permanent loss, and the four claims you must never accept at face value.
limitations: These checks reduce avoidable loss. They do not replace validating a concrete transaction against the validator revision your counterparties run.

pages.title: Status and known limitations
pages.description: What is live, what is beta, what is proposed, what is not exposed at all, and the limitations we know about and have not hidden.
limitations: This page reflects the verified date above. Check the source panel before relying on any row.

pages.title: What are Atomicals?
pages.description: Digital objects that live inside ordinary Bitcoin outputs, identified by the transaction that created them and interpreted by an Atomicals validator.
limitations: The pinned reference revision is one implementation. Another validator version can interpret the same transaction differently.

pages.title: What is ARC-20?
pages.description: The Atomicals fungible token model, where one unit is one coloured satoshi and transfers are an allocation problem rather than an account update.
limitations: Allocation behavior is version sensitive. The numbers on this page follow the pinned reference revision only.

pages.title: Tools
pages.description: Local, read-only tools that model Atomicals behavior without ever signing, broadcasting, or sending your data anywhere.

pages.title: ARC-20 allocation visualizer
pages.description: Model a transaction and see exactly which output receives which units, and what burns, before you build anything.
limitations: Models normal allocation and the activation gated custom coloring path only.
Explanatory. Never a substitute for validating a concrete transaction against your target validator revision.
It never signs, broadcasts, or sends anything anywhere.

pages.title: API explorer
pages.description: Browse every documented operation, parameter, and example, and copy a request to run in your own environment.
limitations: The explorer never sends a request. It renders the contract and produces a command you run yourself.
No credential is embedded, offered, or stored.

pages.title: Bitwork estimator
pages.description: Model a Bitwork prefix and see the expected search space, with the uncertainty stated rather than hidden.
limitations: Probabilistic. Attempts are independent, so a run can finish far under or far over the expectation.
No amount of work guarantees a result in any particular time.
Nothing here estimates cost, revenue, or profitability.

pages.title: CLI command builder
pages.description: Build a validated, copyable command from the pinned command inventory, with the safety implications shown.
limitations: The builder offers only the arguments and options the pinned source declares. A flag absent here is not accepted by that revision.
It builds a string. It never runs anything.

pages.title: Protocol comparison
pages.description: A neutral, source-pinned comparison of Bitcoin metaprotocols, with no rankings, prices, or superiority claims.
limitations: Only the Atomicals and ARC-20 rows are pinned to a source revision read during this review. Other rows describe widely documented design characteristics and are marked as unpinned.
Where a characteristic could not be established from a source read during this review, the cell says unverified rather than guessing.
No row implies that any protocol is better than another. They solve different problems.

pages.title: Transaction safety inspector
pages.description: Parse a transaction or PSBT in your browser and read its inputs, outputs, and signature scope before you sign.
limitations: Parses locally and queries nothing. It cannot know which inputs are coloured unless you supply that.
Explanatory. It is not the active validator and never a substitute for one.
It never signs, broadcasts, or asks for key material.
